title: Sterling Retail - Procurement / MSA & DPA Review
summary: Procurement-led review of Redwood MSA/DPA, discussion of SLAs, data residency, and pricing approval path. Customer requested redlines on MSA, explicit SLA language for latency and uptime, and confirmation of private deployment options (VPC/on-prem). Action items agreed: Redwood to share redlined MSA, security pack, and sample SLA exhibit; schedule follow-up with legal and security next week.
action_items: Evan Brooks - Send redlined MSA and annotated DPA by 2027-01-03
Sofia Martinez - Share security pack (SOC2, ISO docs), KMS integration guide, and architecture diagram by 2027-01-04
Marcus Lee / Sterling - Provide procurement approval timeline and list of required contract owners by 2027-01-05
Victor Alvarez - Confirm whether HSM is required for key material by 2027-01-06
Nina Patel - Send Sterling's standard redline template to Redwood by 2027-01-04
next_steps: Redwood to share updated MSA/DPA and SLA exhibit
Schedule follow-up call with Sterling legal + security (target 2027-01-06)
Run a short latency/cost benchmark on Sterling's EU region for pilot (SE to coordinate)
Provide detailed pricing sheet and committed capacity options within 3 business days
meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-30 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Location: Zoom | Recorder: Fireflies.ai
transcript: 00:00:01 - Evan Brooks: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in right before the holidays. we'll do a run through of the MSA and DPA and then go into SLAs and pricing approvals, sound good?
00:00:12 - Rachel Kim: Yep that works for procurement side we just want clarity on timelines and what will block our legal sign-off, so hopefully today we can get actionable next steps.

00:00:25 - Sofia Martinez: Great, i'll try to keep the technical bits tight. quick intro - i'm Sofia, solutions engineer, i'll cover the architecture and the security attachments. Evan will handle contractual items and pricing.

00:00:40 - Victor Alvarez: Hi, Victor - security architect. main asks: SOC 2 attestation, data residency controls, KMS/HSM support, audit logs and retention. Also curious about private deployment options - we may need a VPC or on-prem for regulated stores in the EU.

00:01:05 - Evan Brooks: Totally understood. On the MSA side, we saw Sterling's initial redlines - thanks for sending those. Our legal team reviewed and we've annotated the MSA. We'll send a redlined version post-call. Any must-have terms from your side, Nina?

00:01:20 - Nina Patel: From legal, liability caps and indemnity language, plus standard data processing language in the DPA. Also need an SLA exhibit with uptime and latency SLOs called out - procurement wants measurable credits for downtime.

00:01:40 - Marcus Lee: On the technical success criteria for pilot - we need sub-150ms 95th percentile for short chat prompts in EU region and cost per 1k tokens under our target. If we move to Dedicated we'll accept better tail latency but need pricing for reserved capacity.

00:02:05 - Sofia Martinez: Ok that's helpful. A couple clarifications: hosted Redwood API in EU region typically hits ~120-140ms p95 for 1-2k token prompts on our curated models; dedicated capacity can improve that and reduce variance. We do have continuous batching and KV cache - that helps for repeated prompts.
00:02:32 - Victor Alvarez: When you say KMS support, do you have HSM-backed keys? Our compliance team might require HSM for certain workloads.

00:02:40 - Sofia Martinez: We integrate with major cloud KMS (GCP KMS, AWS KMS) and can support HSM-backed keys via customer-managed key options. For Private on-prem deployments we can integrate with an on-prem HSM if needed - we should capture that as a follow-up to confirm exact requirements.
00:03:00 - Rachel Kim: Procurement question - what's the approval path on pricing? We need a price table for hosted versus dedicated, and the typical commitment tiers to route to finance.

00:03:10 - Evan Brooks: We'll provide a pricing sheet that maps usage tiers, committed reserved capacity for Dedicated, and discounts for 12/24-month commits. We'll include an example cost estimate for your pilot based on the token volumes you provided earlier.
00:03:30 - Nina Patel: On the DPA, we need explicit data retention periods and deletion guarantees; also confirmation that Redwood won't train models on our data. That clause is a hard stop for us.

00:03:45 - Sofia Martinez: Absolutely - Redwood's hosted offering has a policy where customer data is not used for model training. We'll include the explicit clause in the DPA and the technical controls in the security pack.
00:04:05 - Marcus Lee: For the pilot we'd like to run benchmarks - can Redwood run a short latency/cost test hitting our EU region? we can provide a small dataset and traffic pattern.

00:04:18 - Sofia Martinez: Yes SEs can coordinate; we'll need an IP allowlist or temporary API key. For Dedicated or Private options we can also share performance profiles and be transparent about variance.
00:04:35 - Victor Alvarez: Audit logs and retention - what's typical? We need 12 months of immutable audit logs, and the ability to export them to our SIEM.
00:04:45 - Sofia Martinez: We support export to S3 and integrations with common SIEMs; retention is configurable and we'll include a proposed 12-month policy in the security pack.

00:05:00 - Evan Brooks: Turning to SLAs - typical Redwood hosted SLA is 99.9% uptime for API endpoints with credits in the event of sustained outages. For latency we can include p95 targets in an SLA exhibit, though uptime is the common contractual bit. Are you looking for uptime credits or explicit latency credits?
00:05:18 - Nina Patel: Procurement prefers the legal simplicity of uptime credits, but the product team cares about latency. if you can include a p95 latency target in an appendix that's ideal.

00:05:30 - Evan Brooks: We can do that - we'll draft an SLA exhibit that includes both 99.9% uptime and language for p95 latency targets for your pilot model class. We should be explicit about measurement windows and what constitutes a breach.
00:05:45 - Rachel Kim: Timeline - procurement would like to close by mid-January. Our finance team needs a final pricing sheet and the redline MSA to run it through approvals.
00:05:55 - Evan Brooks: Noted. We'll aim to get the redlined MSA and DPA to you within three business days and the pricing sheet in the same window. Any blockers for that?
00:06:08 - Marcus Lee: One more technical note - we have some PII in inputs for customer support use cases; need clarification on masking and retention for embeddings and logs.

00:06:18 - Sofia Martinez: For embeddings we recommend token-level redaction and can show options: client-side redaction, on-the-fly pseudonymization, or passing through our prefix cache with configured TTL. We'll document recommended patterns in the architecture doc.

00:06:35 - Victor Alvarez: Also need to know about regional failover. If EU region is down, does traffic route to the US by default? we prefer failover to another EU region or a no-failover policy until we approve.

00:06:50 - Sofia Martinez: Smart routing is configurable - by default we route to nearest region for latency, but we can lock routes to EU-only or add explicit fallback policies. We'll include that configuration option in the security/ops doc.
00:07:05 - Nina Patel: Regarding indemnity and liability caps - we will send standard language. Are there any clauses Redwood cannot accept?

00:07:15 - Evan Brooks: We try to be reasonable; for certain open-ended indemnities we may need to negotiate caps aligned with the contract value. We'll flag any non-starters in our redline and propose alternatives.
00:07:30 - Rachel Kim: Ok good. can we confirm who will be the point of contact for legal back-and-forth?
00:07:36 - Evan Brooks: That will be me - i'll loop in our legal counsel as needed. For security specifics, Sofia will take prototype questions and Victor will coordinate with their security owners.
00:07:48 - Marcus Lee: Onboarding - what's a typical timeline from signed contract to pilot running? we want estimates for provisioning dedicated capacity if we choose that path.

00:07:58 - Liam O'Connor: (CSM) Typically 2-3 weeks for a hosted pilot, 4-6 weeks for Dedicated provisioning depending on capacity and region; Private on-prem can be longer depending on networking and HSM setup. We'll capture a ramp plan in the onboarding doc.
00:08:18 - Rachel Kim: For finance, we need an invoice schedule and whether you accept PO / net-30 terms for the pilot stage.
00:08:27 - Evan Brooks: We accept PO and can do net-30 for pilot commitments; for reserved Dedicated contracts we'll need negotiated payment terms - we'll include sample terms in the pricing sheet.
00:08:40 - Nina Patel: Quick question - is there an audit rights clause? Our compliance team typically requires reasonable audit rights and cooperation for assessments.

00:08:48 - Sofia Martinez: Yes we include audit cooperation language and will provide SOC2 reports; for deeper audits we can discuss limited-scope assessments under NDA - we'll surface that in the security pack.
00:09:05 - Evan Brooks: ok we're approaching the top of the hour, want to do a quick recap and assign next steps?
00:09:10 - Rachel Kim: please do, that would be great.

00:09:15 - Evan Brooks: Recap - Redwood to send redlined MSA and annotated DPA with explicit non-training clause; Sofia to share security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS/HSM notes, audit log export); SE to coordinate a short EU-region latency/cost benchmark; Sterling to provide procurement timeline and standard redline template. Follow-up call target 2027-01-06 with legal + security. Anything to add?
00:09:40 - Victor Alvarez: Add confirmation on HSM requirement discussion as action item - i'll confirm if HSM is mandatory.
00:09:45 - Evan Brooks: Noted, Victor will confirm. Great thanks everyone and happy holidays, we'll send the materials early next week.
00:09:55 - Rachel Kim: Thanks all, bye.
00:09:58 - (Recording ends)
